header: L6 · The test architect who has seen coverage lie · sonnet
verdict: Close: 31 of 33 Status A or M findings read as resolved at 8ecfbb2; two are only partly resolved and the delta adds one contradiction and one release-gate collision that would make a guard green without observing it or a PR red for the wrong reason.

findings.section: 10 10.2 (Release and bootstrap, step 1); 10 10.2 (e2e row); S6; plan T088, T103
findings.defect: The R8-10-28 rule that tools/release build refuses when the latest scheduled fuzz.yml run on main is not success does not exempt --dry-run, which the e2e step of every all run calls, needs a GitHub API read that 10 10.1 says nothing but the listed steps may do, and no plan task (T088, T103) carries it as an acceptance line.
findings.scenario: A scheduled fuzz.yml run goes red on a flake or an upstream outage: every PR's e2e step fails with a release refusal, or, offline, with a network error; or the implementer of T103 builds without the check because no acceptance line names it, and S6's release evidence (the success of the latest scheduled run) is then enforced by nothing.
findings.change: In 10 10.2 state that the refusal applies to a non-dry-run build only and name the API read and its token-free form; add the refusal and its fixture (red, green, no run found) to T088's acceptance; keep the e2e dry-run build offline.

findings.defect: The new rule that go generate fails on a spec field that is on neither the gate tags nor the committed ungated list contradicts the text beside it: 01 1.4 says the list today holds sandboxOptions only, while 03 3.2 gives run gate '-' and the I7 Test cell names run among the fields without the tag.
findings.scenario: The generator task lands with only sandboxOptions on the list and go generate fails on run on its first run; or run is quietly added to the list with no approval, and the one list the rule was meant to keep deliberate has an unrecorded member.
findings.change: Put run on the list in 01 1.4 and 03 3.2 with its reason (pane commands run only in the sandbox), or tag it; make the three places name the same members.

findings.defect: The replay of every recorded argv shape against the candidate's sbx is one sentence with no probe id, no result file, no verdict and no stated outcome for a difference, so tools/ci probes and acceptance never see it and a drifted sbx stays green; the replay also covers mutating shapes (sbx env rm, policy allow, secret set) with no scope or cleanup stated.
findings.scenario: The candidate's sbx renames a field in sbx ls --json; the maintainer's block B sitting runs the replay, prints a difference or nothing, and every B1 to B5 result is still pass; acceptance counts probe ids and finds all present.
findings.change: Give the replay an id in 11 11.2 (a B id or a C id) as a kind: check whose observations list each shape and its shape comparison, whose failure names the shape, and which limits the replay to read-only shapes or to the harness's own throwaway sandbox.

findings.defect: The julieta setup no-op bound of 3 s is still asserted in CI on shared hosted runners (median of 5), and no text says what a timing red does, in a spec that forbids skipping flakes; only the romeu half moved to B5.
findings.scenario: A loaded macOS or arm runner reads 3.4 s with no code change; the rule says fix the flake, never skip, so the only move is to raise the bound on that PR.
findings.change: Say in 10 10.1 whether the CI figure gates or is recorded (trend against the previous main run), and what a red means: re-run is not allowed, so name who resets the starting value and through which review.

findings.defect: S9 names five package prefixes while the coverage row says every package go list ./... reports, so e2e/scenarios (and any other e2e package with untagged files) is in the step and out of the criterion, and nothing says whether it counts as 0 percent.
findings.scenario: e2e/scenarios, whose functions run only under the e2e and host tags, shows 0 percent in the untagged race profile and fails the step, or is silently dropped by a filter written from S9.
findings.change: Name e2e/scenarios and e2e/host in S9 and the coverage row as in scope or out, with the reason.

findings.defect: The mutate evidence is the latest scheduled fuzz.yml run on main with no bound on its age or its commit, and GitHub stops scheduled workflows in a repository with no activity for 60 days, so a stale success can stand for a release commit whose guards changed since.
findings.scenario: The schedule is disabled; the last run is a success from before a guard moved; tools/release build accepts it and S6 cites it.
findings.change: Require the run's head commit to be an ancestor of the release commit with no tagged-guard file changed since, or an age bound, in step 1 and in the S6 Evidence cell.

findings.section: spec.md Deferred decisions (a mutation stub per guard site); 05 5.2
findings.defect: The row's trigger, an invariant with a second guard site that a mutate run left unobserved, cannot be seen by a mutate run: one stub per id passes as soon as one tagged test goes red.
findings.scenario: A guard gains a second site; mutate stays green; the trigger never fires and the deferral becomes permanent.
findings.change: Name an observable trigger, for example any invariant whose guard tag appears in two or more functions, counted by tools/ci invariants and printed, or a review reading of that count at each release-candidate tag.

findings.defect: Several round-8 test mechanisms of this lens have no acceptance line in any plan task: the pr rule that removes no last guard or test tag, the zero-test failure of a go test step, the TestTestStyle ban on t.Skip and testing.Short, and the positive controls of I2, I3, I14 and I16 (parked items plan-26 to plan-28 cover only the stub, the absent package and the host vet).
findings.scenario: Each task merges green without its mechanism, and the spec states a gate that the code never had, which is the situation the plan's rule that a task whose named test did not run is not done exists to prevent.
findings.change: Add one acceptance line per mechanism to the task that builds its step, each naming its test by case title.

Parked or L items (plan-9, plan-26 to plan-28, L6-28) are not re-reported. Whether the go list package set matches S9 in practice and how GitHub treats an idle schedule need a run, not the text.
confidence: medium: resolutions were checked by reading the baseline text, not by running tools/ci; the Required findings quote text I read, the Advisory ones rest on inference about runner behavior.
